Aside from focusing on things in your direct experience, you can also suggest yourself into greater alertness (it's still relaxed-alert, not paranoid-alert). Keep your eyes open, and each time you make the auto-suggestion that you're getting clearer, use a small hand movement. Then stop the hand movement and see where your mind is at. That hand movement is the mental escape into the body's flow. Say something like,
“Starting with your eyes open, press your thumb to your forefinger, gently, and let go. Each time you do, you get a little more awake… Press and let go again, a bit clearer. And once more, and now you’re clearer than when you started. Now stop pressing. In the first second after you stop, is the pressing still echoing somewhere? Start with your fingers, which may still be tingling. See if your breath kept the rhythm going, and whether your attention is still waiting for the next press. Or maybe there’s no echo at all. rewrite:
So inner child therapy draws on those higher vantage points more concretely. The inner Guide is the closest thing here to a Higher Self, and it has to work with the Nurturer and Protector and come after them. It can’t act like some transcendent authority that waves everything away. Most reparenting doesn’t do enough with the Guide, which is the opposite extreme from IFS, so I’m trying to bring together the best of both. IFS isn’t exactly one system, so I may be simplifying it here. It has its own branches and disputes, and that’s one more problem I’m trying to remedy by laying all this out systematically in this guide.
IFS calls these wounded young parts “exiles.” I find that pathologizing. I’d rather speak of a child who needs parenting and integration than name them by their wounded or excluded condition.
And the parts just keep coming: managers, firefighters, exiles, polarized parts, legacy burdens, Self-energy, guides, new subparts... At some point it’s a maze, with a little one somewhere in the middle of it. Some practitioners are gentle about it and walk you through the maze just fine, while others seem to leave people more split up than when they started. A big institute and a pile of certificates won’t tell you whether a model is true, or whether it’s safe for you.

As for telling whether it helped, a few hours of feeling lighter, with the old feeling back the same day, is a few hours of relief. I’d take that! I just wouldn’t call the problem solved from it, or give the exercise all the credit, especially if you also slept well for once. Jot down what changed and how long it lasted if you want, and then leave it alone.
How many tries is enough? I really don’t know, and I’d be suspicious of anyone who promises you a number, including you, since some things shift in a day and some take about as long as learning guitar. If it’s making things worse, or you just can’t do it right now, I’d change course sooner (stopping counts). Not wanting to do it anymore is a reason too, but if that “nope” sounds like a part of you that’s trying to protect you, I’d hear it out first. If it still says no, that’s your answer. And if you keep doing the reparenting steps correctly and still don’t get the results you’d expect, ask yourself whether you have a unique case these steps don’t match yet. Maybe you’ll find something that works better for you, or you can ask me what I’d do for this case, or ask a therapist you work with. Either way, I’d like to hear about it!
Sometimes a session goes great, and a few days later you’re skipping lunch and saying yes to everything again. Going deeper next time won’t fix that, because you just haven’t brought any of it out with you yet. To turn this off, stop rehearsing it, take it out of any recordings you have and any apps that are active, and go back to the regular induction you’ve been using. Say that you won’t use it anymore when you’re awake, but just saying it’s gone won’t make it go away immediately. If you find you’re responding to it when you don’t want to, or you’re getting disoriented after using it, get some help from someone qualified. You can keep it in if you want, but only as a way to start a session later, when you want to. For now, today’s trance will be over when you come out of it.
When you come out of it, reverse anything you’ve done to alter your state. If you’ve floated, regain your weight (of your choice, of course), and if you’ve shrunk, grow back to your normal size. If you’ve regressed or met parts, come back to feeling complete in the here and now, and acknowledge that your body belongs to you and is under the control of the adult mind. If you’ve gone somewhere, go back the same way. Etcetera. Make sure the only things you bring out with you are the ones you want to.

When the Practice Feels Real but Stays Shallow
Some people have the opposite problem. It feels like you’re connecting with your little one, but the contact is staying near the surface. Meditating for a long time and then sleeping can open up much more emotionally direct stuff, especially in a second sleep, after you’ve already slept once. I could tell the daytime pl/ork had stayed shallow from the difference at night. If you wake up from a dream soaked in way more feeling and need than anything the session got near, this is probably you. A nice session that just wears off is a different thing. I’d ask what the dream let you feel that the session didn’t, and look at it again after your morning coffee. And if nightmares start wrecking your sleep, dial the practice down by doing it earlier in the day, or for less time.

Notice the Part That Came Here
Some people hear all this about love and answer, “No. I hate myself.” If that’s what you find, just listen to it, without arguing back. But if you opened this article, something in you wanted things to be different, whatever the rest of you was saying. The same goes if you came to therapy or asked someone for help. Or maybe you’d already decided you were hopeless, and then for some reason you tried again.
What was it? It might have been hope, or desperation. Maybe you were curious, or scared. Some people come here out of duty. Or it was more like, “I’m not going to keep suffering like this.” And maybe it was love. Ask that part what it hoped might happen when it brought you here, and follow that thread.

rewrite:
If the Love Isn’t Coming Yet
If you weren’t loved well as a child, “love your inner child” can sound like nonsense. Love them how? Maybe you really want the best for your little one. Maybe you hug them in your imagination, or miss them. And you can still feel none of the warmth people mean when they say love. That doesn’t close the door, though, it just means you start smaller.
Maybe just imagining a caring grown-up makes you feel more threatened, or lonelier. Lonelier is a strange one, with somebody right there. Then go smaller still, to the least cruel response a decent adult could offer your little one. It’s scaffolding, and it isn’t a test of whether you were loved enough.
Taking the hostility out makes room for warmth. What people most often say helped is letting their defenses down. I mean by choice, after the part guarding you has been heard. If you’ve never been safe being loved, your ego can act like a rigid security guard that won’t let the feeling in, and being vulnerable is the opening the feeling needs. (This guard is only about letting the feeling in. People still have to earn your trust.) Sometimes the warmth is there, with a cold part standing in front of it, guarding something. That part tends to step aside once it’s been heard (see the section Hear the Guard First).
If the love still isn’t coming, you can at least stop judging your little one. Obviously no insults. Helpful advice is great, we all need advice. Let them absorb it at their pace. And don’t expect a thank-you for the session, like they booked it. That’s enough to start being the adult, even if it isn’t enough yet for them to trust you. That takes warmth, and if there isn’t any yet, borrow some.
Your little one might not take it well at first. 😜 More like “Oh, so NOW you care?” Your first instinct might be “But I’m trying!” Some days, just hearing it out like a decent adult is the only thing you’ll manage to borrow.

rewrite:
Forgiveness without bypass
We cannot force forgiveness on ourselves. It has to come from a place of understanding, otherwise it can be bypassing. But if we stay in the anger forever, we let the injury dictate how we live our lives in the present. Holding all of this just means remembering that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it. We have to keep our boundary with them, especially after forgiveness, which can weaken it. One day we may find that we have forgiven them for not knowing better, just like Jesus did on the Cross.
You might say to the part of you that got hurt, “I’m not going to use spiritual mumbo jumbo to shush your cries and make you forgive before you're ready. But I’m also not going to build our whole life around this wound forever.”
Forgiving yourself
For self-forgiveness, name what you regret doing, and take responsibility for just that part. Let yourself feel the remorse by taking in the harm done, and see how it went against your values. Just stop short of making yourself a permanent criminal by identifying with the behaviors you're now abandoning.
Do what you can to put it right. Every so often, come back to how you got to be someone who could do that, until you understand the pattern well enough that it can't drive you anymore.
